title: Simple Future — Regular Conjugation
description: Add future endings to the full infinitive to express actions that will happen.

grammar.title: Simple Future (Futuro Simple) — Regular Conjugation
grammar.content:
The future tense expresses actions that will happen, predictions, and promises. Unlike English, Spanish future tense keeps the FULL infinitive as the stem and adds the endings directly — so -AR, -ER, and -IR verbs share the same set of endings.

Future endings (add to the full infinitive):
- yo: -é
- tú: -ás
- él/ella/usted: -á
- nosotros: -emos
- vosotros: -éis
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -án

Examples:
- hablar → hablaré, hablarás, hablará, hablaremos, hablaréis, hablarán
- comer → comeré, comerás, comerá, comeremos, comeréis, comerán
- vivir → viviré, vivirás, vivirá, viviremos, viviréis, vivirán
examples: El año que viene viajaré a España. (Next year I will travel to Spain.)
Mañana compraré pan en la panadería. (Tomorrow I will buy bread at the bakery.)
Creo que lloverá mañana. (I think it will rain tomorrow.)
¿Vivirás aquí mucho tiempo? (Will you live here for a long time?)
grammar.aid_note: Romanian future is built with 'voi/vi/va/vom/veti/va' + infinitive: 'voi vorbi' (I will speak). Spanish is actually simpler — you just add one set of endings to the infinitive, no separate helper verb needed. The Spanish future is one word where Romanian needs two.

pronunciation.title: Stress in Future Endings
pronunciation.content:
Future tense endings all carry the stress on the ending itself:
- yo: -é (always accented)
- tú: -ás (always accented)
- él/ella/usted: -á (always accented)
- nosotros: -emos (no accent — stress on the second-to-last syllable)
- vosotros: -éis (always accented)
- ellos/ellas/ustedes: -án (always accented)

The nosotros form has no accent because the stress naturally falls on the second-to-last syllable, which is the default rule.
pronunciation.aid_note: Romanian future and conditional both place stress on the ending particle. Spanish conjugations naturally place stress on the ending too, so the rhythmic feel is similar.

exercises.question: What is the future form of 'hablar' for 'yo'?
exercises.explanation: 'Hablaré' is the yo form of hablar in the future tense. The ending -é marks first-person singular future.

exercises.question: Which ending is the future 'tú' form?
exercises.explanation: '-ás' is the tú ending in the future tense: hablarás, comerás, vivirás.

exercises.question: Complete: 'El año que viene yo ____ (viajar) a México.' (Next year I will travel to Mexico.)
exercises.explanation: 'Viajaré' — add -é (yo future ending) to the infinitive viajar.

exercises.question: Complete: 'Mañana compraré ____ (bread) en la panadería.'
exercises.explanation: 'Pan' = bread. 'Mañana compraré pan' = Tomorrow I will buy bread.

exercises.question: Complete the future tense conjugation table for the regular verb VIVIR:
exercises.explanation: Future tense adds endings directly to the full infinitive: viviré, vivirás, vivirá, viviremos, viviréis, vivirán.

exercises.question: Which sentence uses the future tense correctly?
exercises.explanation: 'Mañana iré al cine' correctly uses the future tense with a future time marker (mañana = tomorrow).
